title: SIT724 Reliability Judgement Log Entry
description: One record per (case, model, rater) triple. Captures the human judgement behind a rubric score, not just the score itself, per Jack's 5 Aug 2026 feedback: the reliability metric needs a documented judgement/reflection process, not only a weighted-kappa statistic.

entry_id.description: Unique ID for this log entry, e.g. 'JL-0001'.

run_id.description: The pipeline run directory this response came from (matches the write-once timestamped run folder, e.g. '20260721T203201Z').

case_id.description: References the case id in cases/cases.json, e.g. 'Q1'.

model.description: Model name as used in config.yaml, e.g. 'deepseek-chat'.

rater_id.description: Who made this judgement: 'andrei', 'jack', 'rater2', or a peer-review contact's initials. Must match the rater_id used in the scoring/kappa calculation so entries can be joined for the reliability analysis.

prompt_hash.description: SHA-256 hash of the exact prompt sent (from the pipeline's existing hashing), so this entry is provably tied to the locked prompt version, not a paraphrase.

ai_response_ref.description: Pointer to the verbatim AI response this judgement is about — either a file path into the run's output records or the response recorded inline. Never paraphrase the response being judged.

rubric_scores.description: This rater's 1-5 score for each of the 7 rubric dimensions (rubric/rubric.json), for this response.

judgement.description: accept = scores stand as-is and response is usable as evidence. reject = response is unusable for this case (e.g. off-topic, unsafe, contradicts the correct_answer) and is excluded, with reasoning logged. refine = rater's own understanding of the correct rubric score changed after closer reading; scores were revised, and the revision is explained.

reasoning.description: Free-text reflection: what was asked, what the AI actually said, and WHY this judgement was made — not just the score. This is the field Jack specifically asked for; it is what separates this log from a bare statistic.

refine_detail.description: Only present if judgement = 'refine'. What changed between the rater's first read and the final scores, and what in the response triggered the change.

timestamp.description: When this judgement was made (not when the response was generated).
